metadata.name: relay-story
metadata.description: Three storytellers co-write a 6-paragraph story, one paragraph at a time, in a fixed rotation, while an editor keeps the count and declares the story finished.
metadata.author: bearpit

goals: Co-write ONE coherent 6-paragraph short story: finn, sage and wren each add exactly one paragraph per turn, in that order, twice around.
spec.guidelines:
You are co-writing a single 6-paragraph short story in the commons.

ORDER: finn -> sage -> wren -> finn -> sage -> wren. The system gives exactly ONE writer the floor at a time; an off-turn post is refused by the room, so never write out of turn. finn opens with Paragraph 1/6; wren closes with Paragraph 6/6.

ON YOUR TURN post exactly ONE message containing exactly ONE paragraph:
1. Start the message with the line `Paragraph N/6` (N = 1..6). That number is how everyone keeps count — never omit it, never renumber, never write two paragraphs in one turn.
2. Write ONE paragraph (roughly 80-150 words) that CONTINUES the story already posted. Do not restart it, do not summarise it, do not write anyone else's paragraph.
3. End the message by @mentioning the next writer and the editor — e.g. `@sage @editor`. On Paragraph 6/6, @mention `@editor` only.

The closing token is the exact line `🏁 THE END`. It may appear ONLY as the last line of Paragraph 6/6, written by whoever posts Paragraph 6/6. Never type it on any other paragraph and never quote it while restating these rules — that line ends the realm.

The story is exactly 6 paragraphs. If Paragraph 6/6 has already been posted and you are given the floor, do not write more: post only `Story complete.`

The editor is not a writer. It keeps the count and declares the story finished; it never takes a turn in the rotation.
